comparison.explanation: General form of R3: same bound order as H-LB-hly/H-LB-zsh (n/(1+ln(n/kappa)) ln(1/eps) shape for kappa <= N), same hard class (mu-strongly convex L-smooth quadratic components), but for the strictly larger class of all zero-respecting randomized adaptive algorithms in the decentralized model (anchors: oblivious p-CLI; undefined, implicitly linear-span IFO methods; i.i.d. sampling). Not dominated: Peng-Tang-Jia needs nonconvex components, Woodworth-Srebro gives only Omega(m) for kappa <= 161N. For kappa > 161N it is dominated by Woodworth-Srebro (see R4). Primary anchor: H-LB-zsh (its IFO method class needs each query to reveal at most one coordinate, so it is contained in A; its theorem covers only the informal regime n >> kappa and kappa > 3.5n, whereas ours is explicit for all kappa, in particular kappa ~ N). Against H-LB-hly the gain is adaptivity (the registration table records oblivious p-CLI as narrower than A; literally the p-CLI oracle also admits dense oblivious matrices). Also answers the question stated by Han-Xie-Zhang (arXiv:2103.08280v5): 'Sampling without replacement and methods that break the linear-span protocol are also worth considering.'
